catalog_quote: Auf der phonologischen Ebene: [...] Das Pande⁴ hat vier Tonhöhen, sieben Vokale, realisiert ɓ implosiv, aber [ɗ] > l, weist eine Reihe von stimmhaften. Pränasalierten auf und hat eine Opposition p / h, ohne v; [...] Auf der morphologischen Ebene: [...] Das Pande scheint ein mehr reduziertes System von Nominalklassen zu haben (acht Klassen in sechs Klassenpaaren: mò~Ø / bà, mò / mì, mò / mà, ì / lì, lì / bì, lì~dì / mà), eine klassische Verbalableitung, eine vokalische Verbalflexion (perfektiv -i, imperfektiv -a), nicht tonal;

new_statements.translation: On the phonological level: [...] Pande has four tone heights, seven vowels, realises ɓ as implosive but [ɗ] > l, shows a series of voiced prenasalised consonants and has an opposition p / h, without v; [...] On the morphological level: [...] Pande seems to have a more reduced noun-class system (eight classes in six class pairs ...), a classical verbal derivation, a vocalic verbal inflection (perfective -i, imperfective -a), not tonal;

Pranasalierten auf und hat eine Opposition p / h, ohne v' and, under 'Auf der morphologischen Ebene', 'Das Pande scheint ein mehr reduziertes System von Nominalklassen zu haben (acht Klassen in sechs Klassenpaaren..), eine klassische Verbalableitung, eine vokalische Verbalflexion (perfektiv -i, imperfektiv -a), nicht tonal'. A's quote matches apart from bracketed ellipses and scanned renderings of ɓ/ɗ and…
new_statements.relation_note: Four tone heights; seven vowels; implosive ɓ ([ɗ] > l); voiced prenasalised series; p/h opposition without v; verb inflection vocalic, not tonal; 37% lexical agreement with Aka; s (Aka/Ngando) : h (Pande) correspondence.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Pande is described as a tone language with four tone heights (vs. two in Aka, two-to-three in Ngando, four in Mbati); verbal TAM inflection is vocalic (perfective -i / imperfective -a) rather than tonal. Nothing is said about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the only qualification is that verb inflection is 'nicht tonal' (vocalic suffixes), which concerns grammatical tone, not the lexical tone system
new_statements.identity_note: 'Pande' here = Guthrie C12 Pande/Bogongo of the Sangha (CAR), autonym linzéli, listed in Thomas's C10 table as '12a Pande, 12b Bogongo'; the data are the c. 227-item tone-marked QIL 'linzéli (pande)' collected in 1979 by S. Bahuchet — the same language as pand1264 [bkj], not the Cameroonian Grassfields 'Pandé' of Bali. | Guthrie's C.12 Pande with Bogongo (= Glottolog dialects Nuclear Pande and Bogongo of pand1264), '1,000 speakers of Pande alone'. Group-level statement (Bantu Zone C, quoting Guthrie 1948), secondhand. [name in source: Pande (Ndjeli, Linyeli, Linzeli)-Bogongo (Bukongo, Bongili); pages 104-105 (Zone C)]

new_statements.quote: Languages in Zone C share a generally uncomplicated typology according to Guthrie (1948): ",..the principal features of the languages of this zone are a simpler grammatical structure than is found in many others, coupled with a simple phonological and tonal system. [...]" [...] The languages of Zone C are listed below: (10) Ngundi Group (11) Ngondi (Ngundi). (12) Pande (Ndjeli, Linyeli, Linzeli)-Bogongo (Bukongo, Bongili), 1,000 speakers of Pande alone.
